fixes.explanation: Burning is in this passage, friend, but it belongs to the lamb. On the day the sheaf is waved, God says, “you shall offer a year-old lamb without blemish as a burnt offering to the LORD.” The sheaf itself gets waved, not burned. Me, I only burn things by accident, and my cookies have the receipts.

True, friend. The seven days finish, and then God adds one more: “On the eighth day you are to hold a sacred assembly and present a food offering to the LORD. It is a solemn assembly; you must not do any regular work.” Just when you think the feast is wrapping up, there's one more day. It's like finding one last cookie at the bottom of the box.

He waves it, friend. God says, “And he shall wave the sheaf before the LORD so that it may be accepted on your behalf…” So the priest takes the very first of the harvest and lifts it up before the LORD for the people. The timing is set too: “the priest is to wave it on the day after the Sabbath.” If I tried waving a sheaf with this mustache, there'd be grain on my ceiling.

Not yet, friend. God says, “You must not eat any bread or roasted or new grain until the very day you have brought this offering to your God.” The offering comes first, then the eating. Me, I can barely wait ten minutes for a batch to cool, so a rule like this would put my mustache to the test.

Ruby, one of my cookie cutter kids, was the loudest voice in my kitchen, and she's a bell, so I had to look twice at this one. But the text says the day is “…a sacred assembly announced by trumpet blasts.” Bells didn't make the list, friend. Trumpets did.

Clothes never come up, friend. Along with the sacred assembly and the food offering, the instruction is “humble yourselves.” My apron has survived some serious chocolate chip disasters, so I'd have signed up for laundry day happily. But that's not what the text asks.

Fasting isn't in this verse, friend. God says, “And you are to rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.” The harvest is gathered, and the word is rejoice. A fast with my bakery right next door? I'd last about four minutes.

False is right, friend. The last verse says, “So Moses announced to the Israelites the appointed feasts of the LORD.” God had told him to “Speak to the Israelites…” and the chapter ends with Moses announcing the feasts to them. This calendar was not a priests-only memo.
